title: [CQ-R10] Isolated agent lifecycle
description:
Objective: Run coding/QA CLIs in owned attempt workspaces with scoped provider credentials, reconnect and cancellation.

Deliverable: Isolated agent lifecycle. This is task R10 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R09, F10, F11.
definitionOfDone: Agent has no sudo, host credentials or hypervisor authority.
Fresh process/session identity forces full context.
CLI exit/crash preserves artifacts and releases only correct leases.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1-3 (the module) and rows A1-A3. Create scripts/local-runner/agent-lifecycle.mjs, the host side of one isolated agent job. Add the first rows of a new '// CQ-R10 isolated agent lifecycle' section at the end of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs. TDD: write A1-A3 first against a module whose runAgentJob only throws, watch them fail for the right reason, then implement. Stdlib and local-runner imports only, LF line endings, no new dependency.

Header comment (a few lines): one job on an owned VM = job lease, verified sweep, no-mount check, bridge session, verified sweep, lease release. The inputs are trusted host-controller inputs (R06 supplies ownership); every guest byte is untrusted. This is not isolation certification: executionReady is always false and verified-local stays unavailable.

export async function runAgentJob(input). Input keys are exact. Any other key, a sessionId included, is refused, so a caller can neither pick nor reuse a session id. Keys: name, binding, job, daemonInfoPath, forward, onOutput, onObservation, plus optional signal, provider = {}, timeoutMs = 30000 and sleep (passed to endAgentJobs only when given).

Validation, before any daemon or provider call, refusing AGENT_INPUT_INVALID:
- name: isOwnedInstanceName (lifecycle.mjs).
- binding: the probe runGuestSession uses (scopeRequest of a moe.get_context request against it). Keep a frozen copy.
- job: exactly {cli, credential}, credential exactly {name, value}, and jobFrame({cli, role: binding.role, credential}) (R10c, guest-bridge.mjs) must not throw.
- daemonInfoPath: an absolute path with no control character. forward, onOutput and onObservation: functions. signal: undefined or an AbortSignal. provider: a plain record whose run and spawn, when present, are functions and whose executable, when present, is a non-blank string with no control character. timeoutMs: a safe integer from 1 to 60000. sleep: undefined or a function.
- Mint the session id here: `${binding.workerId}@${new Date().toISOString()}#` plus 16 hex characters of crypto.randomBytes(8). Refuse it when it is longer than 255 (the daemon's SESSION_ID_RULE and runGuestSession's cap). A 128-code-point astral workerId exceeds it.
Still with no call:
- an already aborted signal rejects AGENT_ABORTED;
- a name with a job already running in this process rejects AGENT_BUSY. The guard is a module Set, deleted in a finally on every path. It exists because the daemon lease is task-keyed and renews for the same task, so it cannot keep two jobs of one task apart.

Job lease: the R06 lease that cleanupOwned reads, with resourceId jobLeaseResourceId(name).
- Acquire: forward('moe.acquire_resource', {resourceId, taskId, workerId}), exactly those keys, from the binding.
- Lease calls never get the caller's signal. Each gets its own AbortSignal, aborted at timeoutMs, and is raced against that deadline. So a cancelled job still releases its lease, and a hung forward cannot hang the run.
- Parse the MCP result: not isError, exactly one {type:'text'} content item, and its text a JSON object.
- granted true, with lease.taskId and lease.workerId equal to the binding's and a canonical ISO lease.acquiredAt: the lease is held. granted false: reject AGENT_LEASE_BUSY. Anything else (a throw, rejection, timeout, isError or bad shape): reject AGENT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE.
- A rejection means this call holds no lease and ran no provider command. Nothing is released after a refused or unparsed acquire. A lease the daemon granted but this call could not read is left to expiry or to the next run's renewal (fail closed).
- Release: forward('moe.release_resource', {resourceId, workerId, taskId, ifHolderWorkerId: workerId, ifAcquiredAt: acquiredAt}). Never force, never another resourceId, never retried. 'released' only when the parsed result's releasedHolders deep-equals [{taskId, workerId, acquiredAt}]; anything else is 'release-failed'.

Flow after the acquire:
1. Pre-start sweep: endAgentJobs(name, provider) (R10c, guest-session.mjs); a throw counts as unverified. Unverified: no mount probe, no spawn, no release; resolve with failure 'AGENT_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED' and lease 'kept'. This is the reconnect rule: a new job never starts while a process of an earlier job may still run. For example, a controller crash left the lease held, and this acquire only renewed it.
2. assertNoMounts(name, provider) (R09c), then runGuestSession({name, binding, sessionId, job, daemonInfoPath, forward, onOutput, onObservation, signal, provider, timeoutMs}). A rejection becomes failure: its code when it matches /^(?:SESSION|TRANSFER|PROVIDER|LIFECYCLE)_[A-Z0-9_]{1,60}$/, else AGENT_JOB_FAILED. observation stays null, and a mount refusal starts no session.
3. Post-end sweep: endAgentJobs again, on every path that passed step 1, whatever step 2 did. It also kills descendants that a cleanly exited job left behind: decision-cq-r10-split left that policy to this row.
4. lease = verified ? release() : 'kept'. failure = the step-2 code, else 'AGENT_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED' when this sweep is unverified, else null.
5. Resolve Object.freeze({sessionId, observation, failure, terminationVerified, lease, executionReady: false}). Only failure === null means the job ended and no agent process remains. The lease is reported on its own.
Artifacts are never touched. The module runs no delete, stop, purge, restart, mount, transfer or supervisor mode other than bridge. It never writes the R06 ledger and never removes the workspace or a session home. Output reaches onOutput as it arrives.
Error handling: refusals are agentError(code) with fixed text. A message never carries the credential, a path, a guest byte or upstream text.

Test harness. Reuse GUEST, owner, scratch, fakeGuest, healthy, guestDetail, mountinfo, Writable, PassThrough, EventEmitter, encodeFrame, createFrameDecoder and MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES. Add this section's own imports at its top, as the R09c section does.
- SECRET: 32 characters from [\x21-\x7e]. JOB = {cli:'claude', credential:{name:'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', value: SECRET}}. AGENT = {role:'worker', workerId:'worker-1', ...owner}.
- PKILL and PGREP: R10c's exact argv, ['exec','--no-map-working-directory', GUEST, '--', 'sudo', '-n', 'pkill', '-KILL', '-U', 'moe-agent'], and the same with 'pgrep', '-U', 'moe-agent'. Pin them literally, as a cross-check of R10c.
- run: info and mountinfo go to fakeGuest. PKILL and PGREP answer from scripted exit codes: 0 resolves, and any other code rejects like execFile with {code, stdout:'', stderr:''}. Anything else is recorded as unexpected and throws.
- A spawn-compatible fake bridge, modelled on fakeProvider in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. It records stdin and decodes the host frames. Once the job frame arrives, it sends hello and scripted guest requests (moe.get_context, moe.start_step), waits for their replies, sends the exit observation and exits 0. It exits 74 when stdin closes early.
- forward: routes moe.acquire_resource and moe.release_resource to scripted MCP results, {content:[{type:'text', text: JSON}]}. It records every call with its signal, and answers guest tools with a small JSON object.
- A daemon.json with no bindHost, written in scratch(t).

Rows:
- A1, refusals before any call. Each invalid input above rejects AGENT_INPUT_INVALID: a wrong name; an architect role; a null binding; missing or extra job keys; cli 'gemini'; OPENAI_API_KEY for claude; an empty, 4097-character, space or control-character value; a relative daemonInfoPath; a non-function forward, onOutput, onObservation or sleep; a null provider or one with spawn 'x'; timeoutMs 0, 60001 or '100'; signal {}; an extra sessionId key; the astral workerId. An aborted signal rejects AGENT_ABORTED. Every case makes zero forward, run and spawn calls, and its error message contains neither SECRET nor a path separator.
- A2, the lease.
  - granted false rejects AGENT_LEASE_BUSY.
  - Each of these rejects AGENT_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE: a rejection; a synchronous throw; isError; two content items; non-JSON text; a lease for another taskId or workerId; a non-canonical acquiredAt; a forward that never settles (timeoutMs 50).
  - Each case makes exactly one forward call, ('moe.acquire_resource', {resourceId: GUEST, taskId, workerId}), with a signal that is not the caller's, and no run, spawn or release call.
  - Busy: while run 1 waits in its acquire, run 2 on the same name rejects AGENT_BUSY with no call of its own. Once run 1 settles, run 3 reaches its acquire.
- A3, a clean job.
  - The run calls are exactly [PKILL, PGREP, info, mountinfo, PKILL, PGREP]. The one spawn, ['multipass', bridgeArgv(GUEST), {shell:false, windowsHide:true, stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']}], comes between mountinfo and the second PKILL.
  - The first stdin frame deep-equals {kind:'job', version:1, cli:'claude', role:'worker', credential:{name:'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', value: SECRET}}, and its bytes equal jobFrame's. The other stdin frames are only the replies.
  - The forward calls are exactly: the acquire; get_context with {taskId, workerId, sessionId}; start_step with the attempt identity and the same sessionId; then the release with {resourceId, workerId, taskId, ifHolderWorkerId, ifAcquiredAt}.
  - The result deep-equals the frozen {sessionId, observation, failure:null, terminationVerified:true, lease:'released', executionReady:false}. sessionId matches /^worker-1@\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z#[0-9a-f]{16}$/.
  - SECRET appears in no forward argument, no run or spawn argument or option, and not in JSON.stringify of the result.
Keep the tests safe on Node 18 and 20 (no Promise.withResolvers, no AbortSignal.any). Use only in-process fakes, so the A-rows run unskipped on Windows, macOS and Linux.

DoD 2-3 and rows A4-A6. Add these rows to the CQ-R10 section, and fix whatever they expose in agent-lifecycle.mjs. Each row asserts the exact run, spawn and forward call lists, so a missing sweep, an extra command or a stray release fails it.
- A4, a crash is data.
  - The observations {code:null, signal:'SIGSEGV'} and {code:137, signal:null} each resolve with failure null, that observation and lease 'released'.
  - Lingering descendants: a post-end PGREP that answers 0 and then 1 runs PKILL twice and still verifies.
  - Output frames sent before the observation reach onOutput as bytes.
- A5, failures release only the right lease.
  - (a) The session fails, then a verified post-end sweep releases. failure is the session's code, observation is null and lease is 'released'. Rows: provider exit 3 (SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED); a second hello (SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION); the caller aborting after hello (SESSION_ABORTED). In the abort row the fake forward rejects any call whose signal is already aborted, so the release proves lease calls never carry the caller's signal. Output sent before the provider crash still reached onOutput.
  - (b) The post-end sweep is unverified: PGREP answers 0 on every round, PGREP exits 2, or PKILL hits a provider error. terminationVerified is false. failure is AGENT_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED after a clean observation, or the session's code after a failed one. lease is 'kept', with no release call at all.
  - (c) The pre-start sweep is unverified: failure AGENT_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED, lease 'kept', and no info, mountinfo, spawn or release call.
  - (d) Mounts: a provider mount or a 9p line gives TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT, and an empty mountinfo gives TRANSFER_MOUNTS_UNKNOWN. There is no spawn, then a verified post-end sweep and lease 'released'.
  - (e) The release is refused: isError; empty releasedHolders; releasedHolders naming another acquiredAt; a rejected forward; a hang past timeoutMs. Each gives lease 'release-failed' with exactly one release call, never retried and never with force.
- A6, reconnect and a fresh identity.
  - Run 1 ends SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED with an unverified post-end sweep (lease 'kept').
  - Run 2 of the same binding gets the same renewed lease, with the same acquiredAt, as the daemon renews per task. It runs PKILL and PGREP before its spawn, starts a new job (a new bridge spawn; nothing is reattached), and releases with run 1's acquiredAt.
  - Across five runs every sessionId is distinct and matches the shape. Each run's guest get_context and start_step carry that run's id, never an earlier one.
  - The daemon then refuses step entry for a new session until it reads moe.get_context: CONTEXT_RECEIPT_STALE in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/executionAuthorization.ts, covered by tools/startStepAuthorization.test.ts ('a receipt for another session'). That is how a fresh id forces a full context read; do not duplicate that daemon test here.
- Allowed commands: collect every run and spawn argv across A3-A6, and assert each is one of bridgeArgv(GUEST), the info argv, the mountinfo probe, PKILL or PGREP. So there is no delete, stop, purge, restart, mount, transfer, materialize or export.

Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff, the final step. Load the adversarial-self-review skill and read the diff as an attacker.
- Concurrency: two runs of one name in one process (the guard); two names in parallel; a run racing its own abort.
- Ordering: no spawn before a verified pre-start sweep; no release before a verified post-end sweep; every release pinned with ifAcquiredAt; the guard removed on every path, throws included.
- Credential confinement: SECRET only inside the job frame. Never in an error, a result, a forward argument, an argv, spawn options or a log.
- Hostile answers: a daemon result with extra keys, a toJSON hook, a getter or a huge text must not get past the parse. A guest that floods output or never exits is bounded by runGuestSession and the caller's signal.
State these residuals in the completion summary:
- The task-keyed lease cannot keep same-task jobs in two processes apart. The in-process Set covers one process; one controller per seat covers the rest.
- A busy acquire leaves a daemon queue entry, which may later grant this task an unused lease. That only delays cleanupOwned (fail closed).
- Termination evidence is the pgrep probe, not a kernel guarantee. pkill -U moe-agent also reaches setsid descendants, which keep the uid.
- No real VM, Multipass or sudo ran; that is R13's certification.
If this review changes code, re-run step 3's gate and use that output.
Rails: no Git-write commands (wrappers land), no .moe edits, no verified-local or isolation claim; executionReady stays false.
Then call complete_task with the gate output and this DoD map:
- DoD1: A3's credential confinement and allowed commands, and A5d's mount refusal, on top of R07's identity probes and R10b's privilege drop.
- DoD2: A6 plus the daemon receipt gate.
- DoD3: A4, A5 and the allowed-command check.
- DoD4: the gate.

comments.author: worker-3729a0d6
comments.content:
Handoff from CQ-R08 (task-7a77465621dc4d6588d5747394cb0ced, host session in scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs), for planning R10 cancellation and teardown:
1. Signal teardown of the guest supervisor is still open; R08b's QA note deferred it here. A SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGKILL sent to guest-supervisor.py skips its finally, and the job's start_new_session group survives. Observed locally: a supervisor SIGKILLed during an R08 mutation run left its job orphaned under init. Today only host EOF (exit 74) and I/O errors kill and reap the group.
2. On abort, runGuestSession closes the bridge stdin and waits up to timeoutMs, then SIGKILLs the local provider process (multipass exec). That local kill does not prove the guest job ended, and executionReady is always false. R10 needs guest-side termination evidence, such as a job table or a kill-and-verify step.
3. The session resolves only on a provider exit 0 with exactly one observation. Every other end rejects with a fixed SESSION_* code.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Put lease and termination handling inside runGuestSession. Rejected: guest-session.mjs is the R08/R10c bridge transport. Daemon lease calls and sweeps there would couple protocol to lifecycle and grow R10c's file.
2) Inject lease callbacks, like cleanupOwned's leaseHeld. Rejected: the release must pin the daemon's exact lease (ifHolderWorkerId plus ifAcquiredAt from the acquire result). Calling moe.acquire_resource and moe.release_resource through the existing trusted forward makes that pinning testable, with no unwired seam.
3) Reconnect by reattaching to a running guest job. Rejected: R10a's supervisor kills the job on host EOF, and the bridge has no resume. A reconnect is a new job with a fresh session id, after a verified sweep.
4) Kill lingering descendants inside the supervisor on a normal completion. Rejected for this row: decision-cq-r10-split left that policy here, and the host-side post-end sweep (R10c endAgentJobs) covers it with no further supervisor change.
5) Re-run R07's identity probes before each job. Rejected: readiness proves them at boot, and nothing in the guest can grant moe-agent sudo afterwards. DoD1 rests on R07 plus R10b plus this row's confinement of credential, mounts and commands.
6) Put the tests in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Rejected: DoD 4 names local-runner.test.mjs, which also holds fakeGuest and the mount fixtures.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- jobLeaseResourceId(name) (lifecycle.mjs:75) is the daemon resource lease that cleanupOwned reads. This row acquires and releases it around one agent job.
- Daemon leases are task-keyed. acquire_resource (tools/acquireResource.ts) requires the task's assignee, and renews an existing lease of the same task with acquiredAt unchanged (state/resourceStore.ts:191). release_resource (tools/releaseResource.ts) takes ifHolderWorkerId and ifAcquiredAt preconditions and returns releasedHolders [{taskId, workerId, acquiredAt}]. MCP results are {content:[{type:'text', text: JSON}]} (server/McpAdapter.ts:309).
- runGuestSession (guest-session.mjs:39) validates its own input. It stamps sessionId onto get_context, and {attemptId, generation, sessionId} onto start_step, complete_step and complete_task (STAMPED). It always rejects with a fixed SESSION_* code.
- assertNoMounts (snapshot-transfer.mjs:67) is the info call plus the mountinfo probe, both through provider.run.
- The step-entry receipt gate in util/executionAuthorization.ts compares the receipt's sessionId; see startStepAuthorization.test.ts:170, 'a receipt for another session'. Session id rule: at most 255 characters, no NUL, CR or LF (attemptStore.ts:385, moe-proxy README).
- Test helpers in local-runner.test.mjs: nameAt and owner (~284-287); GUEST (906); scratch (299); fakeGuest (989); healthy, guestDetail, mountinfo, MOUNTS, SHARED_LINE and HOST_MOUNT (~950-990); Writable (1615); the R09c imports (2688+). Model the fake bridge on fakeProvider in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (~616).
- ASSUMED interfaces, unlanded, taken from the R10b and R10c task contracts:
  (a) R10c: runGuestSession's input gains job {cli, credential:{name, value}}. It writes jobFrame's bytes first on stdin, and an invalid job gets SESSION_INPUT_INVALID before spawn.
  (b) R10c: endAgentJobs(name, provider = {}, {rounds = 3, sleep, delayMs}) in guest-session.mjs resolves a frozen {verified}. It runs through lifecycle's invoker (provider.run): 'exec --no-map-working-directory <name> -- sudo -n pkill -KILL -U moe-agent', then the same with 'pgrep -U moe-agent'. verified is true only on pgrep exit 1.
  (c) R10c: guest-bridge.mjs exports jobFrame({cli, role, credential}) and AGENT_JOBS. claude takes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; codex takes OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY. A value is 1-4096 characters of [\x21-\x7e]. Refusals are BRIDGE_* codes that never echo the credential.
  (d) R10b: the guest frame {kind:'job', version:1, cli, role, credential}, and the guest side (moe-agent, cwd WORKSPACE, a fresh session home, the env allowlist). This row never calls R10b code directly.
  If a landed name or shape differs, follow the landed code, keep the behavior these rows pin, and note the delta in the step note (moe.amend_plan_step if material).
planningNotes.risks:
- Same-task concurrency: the lease is task-keyed and renews for the same task, so it cannot keep two jobs of one task apart. The in-process Set covers one process, and one controller per seat covers the rest. State this as a residual.
- A busy acquire enqueues the task in the daemon. A later grant may leave this task holding an unused lease until it expires or the next run releases it. That only delays cleanupOwned (fail closed); do not add queue cleanup.
- Lease calls must never use the caller's signal. A cancelled job must still release, and a hung forward must be bounded by timeoutMs.
- Never release unless the post-end sweep verified, and never after a refused or unparsed acquire. A lease granted but unparsed stays held (fail closed).
- Unverified termination after a clean observation is still a failure (AGENT_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED). A caller exporting the workspace while an agent process may run would read a moving tree.
- The minted session id must fit in 255 UTF-16 units. An astral workerId of 128 code points does not.
- R10c drift: pin PKILL, PGREP and the job frame literally, so a contract change fails loudly.
- Tests must stay Node 18 and 20 safe (no Promise.withResolvers, no AbortSignal.any). Inject sleep instead of waiting on real retry delays.
- A job longer than the lease's maxLeaseMs (24 h by default) loses it to the reaper, and its release then reports 'release-failed'.
- Size: at most 400 changed lines across the two files, with no size exception. R09 final also edits local-runner.test.mjs; dependsOn keeps the two serialized.
- Cross-platform: this is host code only (spawns use shell:false, and the only host path is daemonInfoPath). The A-rows use in-process fakes, so they run on Windows, macOS and Linux.
